survive the godling's brand; choose what to do with the mark.

quests.title: The One Who Climbed Beside You

steps.objective_text: survive the rival's ambush; decide their fate (the sticky-outcome fork).
push one of your own creatures to a pure force-pole and complete the Apotheosis ritual — make your first minor god.
defeat a chosen Olympian (god-rank Act boss) and claim its domain.
accept or refuse a god's Faustian alliance against its rivals.
confront the minor god you made in Act 2, now turned by the thrones; reclaim, re-kill, or free it.
complete your deicide spree to the threshold that wakes the Primordials; accept the final Marker.
face the six pure poles — pass them (Ascension/God-Maker) or kill them (Unmaking).

quests.title: The Last Reckoning of the Clans

steps.objective_text: resolve the final clan war at the foot of the throne — your faction as ally or last obstacle.
marshal (or face) every thread you've left live across the run for the throne-room approach.
make the run-defining Choice at the empty seat.
undergo the snapshot — your champion + pantheon crystallized into a Dead God world-boss.
fight the climber as the Dead God — the wall the whole game taught you to break, now manned by you.
decide your link in the Succession — crush, step aside, or break the chain.
witness the closing of your link in the Succession; read the run's last line.

A street child's "legendary" — a very confident pigeon — has survived three encounters and gained a scar. Whistle, the kid's reluctant accomplice, begs you to enter the bird in a real Arena warm-up so the child will finally stop selling tickets.

quests.title: What the Tent Keeps Count Of

steps.objective_text: Cessil's tent "keeps count" of something she won't name. She'll tell you what — for a price you pay in a small, true thing about yourself — if you first retrieve the other deck from her mute twin, "Other-Cessil," in the tent's mirror.

Forty has a sealed memo he can't deliver — the recipient embassy keeps moving the door. Run it for him, to whichever of the Nine the seal belongs to (the seal is smudged; you'll have to read the faction's wax-mark to know).

Dree sold a "blessed" melon — technically alive, technically grateful — and the buyer returned it, weeping, because it purrs and will not be eaten. Dree needs you to find the melon a home: a creature that'll bond with it, or a Bloomwarden who'll take it in, or a quiet patch of soil to plant it before sundown ("don't make eye contact past sundown").

Ona wants to prove the soft creed works: breed a Budwarden line through to a Boughtender carrying the recessive "six-petal" trait (a purely cosmetic mark the Bloomwardens treasure), raising the offspring in the Glut so the ground tints them Eros.

A wild Greenwatcher (Eros/Thanatos, jungle-stalker apex) has been dragging living Bloomwarden patients out of the Last-Bloom Hospice and "planting" them in the deep fringe — not to kill, but to fold them into the cycle early. Wenlow wants it stopped, and — because she's a Bloomwarden — not killed if you can manage it.

Trousseau has waited at the Unconsummated Chapel for centuries for a groom the Pale Court says was "reassigned to a vault." Find out what actually happened to him — a thread that leads into the Court's ledger and the truth of a very old, very quietly settled debt.

Cinda burns the dead properly — no reanimation, no withdrawal, no terms — and the Steward hates her for the waste. She's running low on pyre-oil that the Court keeps "losing" in transit. Escort a shipment of consecrated oil from Threshold's docks to the Last Pyre, past Collector Veum's "spot inspections."

quests.title: A Good One, Before the Rust

steps.objective_text: Doubt — a construct that woke to its own atrocities and can't stop malfunctioning about it — has room for one more directive before the rust takes it, and it begs you to make that last act a gentle one. Give it a final task that is not harm.

Bel keeps the Memorial of Hands — the thousand mortal workers bricked into Hephaestion's great works as load-bearing fill, whom no faction grieves. She asks one thing: recover the worker-rolls from a sealed foundry wing the Guild abandoned, so the names aren't lost when she dies with them.

Nim has flagged a batch of Guild-issue constructs as "out of tolerance by point-three" and condemned them to the rendering pits — but suspects the real fault is upstream sabotage, not the units. Hunt down the source of the drift (a tampered blueprint) before a hundred salvageable constructs hit Slag-Master Bohm's bench.

The Untethered Tap detached from the mainland a century ago and can't land — Castellan Mio won't clear "unregistered airspace." Wend asks you to navigate the High Table's landing-clearance bureaucracy on his behalf, or find a flight-capable creature strong enough to tow the island to a registered dock.

A sky-rival aspirant — "hates your guts, owes me money" — has a loosed signature creature terrorizing the lower sky-reaches: a Skyrender wyvern (Ouranos flight-apex). Vane wants the rival brought in breathing (double pay) and the wyvern off his board.

Ode has impounded a smuggler's entire caravan over a single undeclared sandwich and the paperwork is now ruining her week. She'll release the genuinely useful contraband she doesn't care about (a relic, a mutagen) if you'll resolve the dairy incident — track down whether the sandwich was, in fact, declared, by interviewing a chain of increasingly evasive sky-vendors.

quests.title: The Map That Was True Once
quests.giver_npc: The Cartographer of Nowhere, Wess Mapless

steps.objective_text: Wess maps the Sunder; the Sunder disagrees. He's one map behind reality and knows it — but he's convinced there's a fixed point somewhere in the warp (a place the chaos can't re-tile) and asks you to walk his last-true map to its center and confirm whether the fixed point exists. (It leads to The Last Sane Man, Hewes Stillmind, and his shrinking circle.)

Glum, the Long Party's one sober witness, is exhausted and needs a night off — but the Revel's door moves and someone has to mark it for the lost. Cover Glum's shift: stand at the (moving) door, warn the arrivals about the red one, and witness the party so Glum doesn't have to.

Bress will share a Stoneblood breeding-line only if you prove you breed for truth, not power: surface a named rare recessive in a World Tortoise (Worldback) lineage over generations, raising the offspring on Mordathun's back so the Old Weight tints them Gaia-deep. (A lesser, single-line echo of the main-quest "Six Generations Deep," gated to a different recessive and reward.)

Doun has preached for forty years that Mordathun, the Old Weight, is merely sleeping and will wake — and the clans humor him. He's felt a new "breath" in the Fallen Hill and begs you to descend the Sermon-Scar and confirm whether the dead Titan stirs, or whether it's just a frightened old man and the wind. (Touches the deep-strata; complements but does not trigger the main-quest "Old Weight Wakes.")

Vrenna keeps the only fire in Titanfall for the clanless — the exiles cast out for taking the fast path (like R999 Driftblood). Her halfway-house is running short on everything, and the clans won't fund "cheaters." Provision the outer-scree fire, and help her coax one specific bitter exile (Driftblood) back to the bowl.

quests.title: Oil for the Dry Tower
quests.giver_npc: The Lighthouse-Keeper of the Dry Tower, Old Marrow Highwick

steps.objective_text: Highwick keeps a lighthouse burning for a sea that no longer moves — not for ships, but to remind the deep that up still exists and hold the hymn back from the tower. He's out of oil, and the thing circling his light in the dark is getting bolder. Bring him oil, and drive off (or pacify) the Brineherald (Ouranos/Thanatos reef-folk) that's been dousing his beacon.

Mell sends bottled messages up to the surface — and the deep keeps intercepting them, reading them, replying in Mell's own handwriting. Mell asks you to carry one real bottle, uncorked by human hands, to the surface — and to find out who below is forging the replies. (Leads to a deep-secret about what the Choir's communion actually does to a sender's tenses.)

Pell is a Choir initiate not yet fully changed — still one voice, still grieving the plural to come. Before the deepening takes the last of his single self, he asks one thing: help him do a single surface thing — feel sun, eat food that someone cooks, hear his own name said by someone who isn't the deep — one last memory to hold as the we closes over him.

Imo seals wild creatures lawfully, perfectly — and has lately, in heresy, started leaving each seal a hair loose, a gap the bound thing could work at given a century. She's afraid she'll be caught. She asks you to carry a message to Brother Recant (the Concord jurist losing his faith) and to help her un-seal one specific creature she can't bear to have bound.

quests.title: The Wild Saint's Cousin
quests.giver_npc: Sealwright-Adept Simca of the Eighth Seal

steps.objective_text: A lesser Cosmos creature — kin to the feral "Wild Saint" of the main quest — has gone unsealed and rampaging through the regulation gardens, undoing four hundred years of order one straight line at a time. The Concord wants it contained, not killed (waste offends the law). Bring it in lawfully.

quests.title: Her Name, Every Day
quests.giver_npc: The Curator of the Almost-Forgotten, Mam Threnody

steps.objective_text: Mam Threnody tends the Gallery of What's Left — the half-names and faces the Rot hasn't finished eating. She keeps the real name of the Accreted Woman (the creature wearing the half-remembered shape of someone who fell in) and gives it to her daily, for one moment of being whole, before the Rot takes it back. Threnody is failing; she asks you to learn the name and carry the ritual on, or to find out who the Accreted Woman was — and whether you met her above.

quests.title: The Optimist's Tea
quests.giver_npc: The Optimist of the Abyss, Glad Wennick

steps.objective_text: Glad Wennick is relentlessly cheerful at the bottom of everything, in a decorated ledge-hovel, with a twitching god-finger on the wall "for the view." His tea-kettle (one of his few comforts) has been swallowed by a Rot-pool, and he asks you — brightly — to fetch a replacement from Gristle's salvage stall and stay for a cup, because the Rot can't eat a smile and he'd like to test that theory with company.

quests.title: One Honest Tap
quests.giver_npc: The Inspector Who Can't Get In, Emissary Brass-Knock

steps.objective_text: An Iron Guild emissary has been knocking on a door that leads nowhere — the Atelier won't open to anyone but the hand that built it — for six days, on Magna Ironwright's orders, to "tour your player-authored realm (for envy, mostly envy)." Brass-Knock can't get in and won't leave. He asks only that, if you ever build something especially fine inside, you tap the door once so he knows the Guild's dream is real.

Offcut — a helper the Atelier assembled from your discarded attempts, your trimmings, the almosts you scrapped — points you to the Unfinished Wing, where the Unmade drift: the murmuring echoes of every creature you melted, sacrificed, or abandoned, asking only whether they were worth the making. Offcut begs you to finish the wing by deciding their fates. (This is the side-quest face of the main-quest "Unfinished Wing" set-piece — scoped to a single wing and a lesser reward, not the full God-Maker production tier.)
